element.description: Use this wording for element-of-leverage pages where completion means shipped output.

jobToBeDone.title: Complete a Coding Task using Synchronous AI assistance
jobToBeDone.body: Developers use GitHub Copilot to complete coding tasks within their editor and terminal.

whatCountsAsCompletion.title: A PR opened by a Copilot-active developer
whatCountsAsCompletion.body: Valid = Developer opened a PR for review. Failed/flawed = PRs closed without merging are subtracted from valid completions.

jobClass.title: Value-creating
jobClass.body: Valid completions create valuable work product.

efficiency.description: Use this wording for efficiency pages where the task boundary is the coding task itself and the main question is how many saved dev-hours are implied relative to dev-hours invested.

jobToBeDone.title: Complete a Coding Task using Synchronous AI assistance
jobToBeDone.body: Developers use GitHub Copilot to complete coding tasks within their editor and terminal.

whatCountsAsCompletion.title: A PR opened by a Copilot-active developer
whatCountsAsCompletion.body:
Valid = Developer opened a PR for review. 
Failed/flawed = PRs closed without merging are subtracted from valid completions.

jobClass.title: Value-creating
jobClass.body: Valid completions create valuable work product.

howEfficiencyImproves.title: Developers use GitHub Copilot to improve Coding results, or reduce Coding resource consumption.
howEfficiencyImproves.body:
Efficiency can show up if a completion 
1) consumes fewer dev-hours, 
2) encounters less risk, 
3) is larger in size, scope, or difficulty, and/or 
4) consumes fewer dollars than otherwise would have been required without Copilot.

estimatesAndAssumptions.title: Conversion factors allow activity, usage, and output to estimate saved dev-hours
estimatesAndAssumptions.body:
The hours spent is modeled as a stable percentage of Total Dev Capacity(reflecting a decision to keep dev capacity stable). 
The hours saved is modeled based on 3 factors: 
1) Activity level of Copilot Usage, 
2) Lines of Code accepted from Copilot, 
3) Fixed productivity gain per dev-day of usage (reflecting the expected impact of improving average usage levels).

indicatorsOfProgress.title: The Average levels of copilot metrics correlate to efficiency gains
indicatorsOfProgress.body:
Activity, lines of code accepted, and dev days of usage are used to estimate time savings. 
These estimates reflect the magnitude of  efficiency gains and opportunity for improvement .
When the modeled time savings based on these indicators agree, we have higher confidence in the time saved estimates.

structural.description: Use this wording for pages whose purpose is to describe structural conditions, coverage, and consistency rather than saved-hour estimates.

jobToBeDone.title: Expand the structural conditions for AI-assisted coding
jobToBeDone.body: This view examines how broadly and consistently AI-assisted coding is present across developers, pull requests, and lines of code.

whatCountsAsProgress.title: Broader and more consistent evidence of AI-assisted coding
whatCountsAsProgress.body: Progress appears as higher adoption, higher PR-assisted share, higher AI-assisted LoC share, and more stable day-to-day coverage across the observed population.

jobClass.title: Structural
jobClass.body: Structural improvement does not directly create output by itself. It expands the conditions under which efficient work can occur across more developer-hours and more workflows.

howStructuralImprovementImprovesOutcomes.title: Higher number of devs, completions, and percentage of work improved all expand and ultimately limit realized benefit from efficiency gains.
howStructuralImprovementImprovesOutcomes.body: These are the structural factors that determine how broadly efficiency gains are realized across the organization.

estimatesAndAssumptions.title: The value used for 100% is configured for % Adopted; other dimensions use measured values for 100%.
estimatesAndAssumptions.body: These metrics are based on observed adoption, PR classification, and LoC classification. They are structural indicators, not labor-savings estimates.

indicatorsOfProgress.title: Completeness metrics show the opportunity and progress for different structural dimensions.
indicatorsOfProgress.body: Structural progress can be viewed in terms of completeness across dimensions such as % Adoption, % Assisted PRs, % Assisted Lines of Code, etc.
